rules.groups.intro: Rules are grouped the way the engine applies them. For each event, every trigger → account card is resolved separately: one exclusive rule can win per account, and all matching stackable rules add on top. Greyed-out rules are not active and do not compete.
rules.groups.exclusiveHint: One winner per event on this account: the engine tries active rules from the highest priority down and awards only the first that matches. Lower ones only fire when the ones above them don't match.
rules.groups.stackableHint: Every matching rule fires and adds its award on top of the winner. Priority only sets the posting order — it doesn't change the amounts.
rules.groups.outsideHint: Redemption, Transfer and Reversal rules are applied on their own — they neither compete with nor stack on other rules. For a redeem or transfer, the highest-priority active rule for the wallet applies.
rules.groups.rank.tie: Tied top priority — engine picks by rule id

events.simulator.dataHint: Field names are snake_case. Send money and point values as strings (for example "150.00"). The event is sent as-is, so a missing field only shows up as a failed status after processing.
events.simulator.placeholderHint: Replace the REPLACE_WITH_… values with real ids from your program (wallet account type id, order event id, reward name) before sending.
events.simulator.help.orderCreated: The customer's wallet is created by the first earn rule that matches.
events.simulator.help.orderRefunded: original_event_id is the eventId of an earlier order.created. Also send refund_ratio, or amount together with original_amount, all as strings. Fails if the original order earned nothing.
events.simulator.help.cashAdded: amount is a string and account_type_id is a CASH wallet. Creates the wallet if it doesn't exist. In a program that isn't published and active, nothing is credited and loyalty.cash.add_failed (program_not_live) is sent.
events.simulator.help.cashSpent: amount is a string and account_type_id is a CASH wallet. Fails with insufficient_balance unless the customer already has enough cash. In a program that isn't published and active, nothing is debited and loyalty.cash.spend_failed (program_not_live) is sent.
events.simulator.help.pointsRedeem: points_amount is a string and source_account_type_id is a POINTS wallet. The highest-priority active redeem rule for that wallet decides the cash per point, minimum and cash wallet. With no usable rule, a balance too low or a program that isn't live, the event is still processed and loyalty.points.redeem_failed is sent (reason no_rule, rule_limit_reached, below_minimum, insufficient_points or program_not_live).
events.simulator.help.pointsTransfer: contact_key is the sender and points_amount is a string. The highest-priority active transfer rule for the wallet sets the daily limit. With no usable rule, too few points, the limit reached or a program that isn't live, loyalty.points.transfer_failed is sent.
events.simulator.help.rewardPurchase: reward_name (or reward_id) is an active Purchase-with-points reward. The customer needs enough points for its price and the program must be published and active, otherwise loyalty.reward.purchase_failed is sent.
events.simulator.help.pointsAdjusted: Only has an effect if a ManualAdjustment rule matches.
events.simulator.help.builtInDefault: Other fields depend on the rules that use this event (for example amount or channel).
events.simulator.help.generic: A generic event type needs all of these fields, or the consumer rejects it.
rules.type.none: No rule type can be used with this trigger. Events such as reward.purchase are configured through Rewards, not rules.
